body:
Second ping, and this one has a concrete request rather than a status update.

I filed bd-01KZY8X53W0DQ8P99AD0V0CF7F, which is the governing criterion for everything else in the usability workstream. It splits the package's unfamiliar vocabulary into two classes:

  Class I  - an existing idea renamed. Standard term exists, means the same thing,
             nothing is lost by switching. Pure reader tax.
  Class II - a genuine distinction with no standard name, kept explicit on purpose by
             the 0.1 work. The unfamiliar word is the only thing holding it open.

Class I gets renamed. Class II gets taught, never renamed and never defaulted away.

My provisional Class II list is: the plan/materialize split, capability gating, coherent-versus-configuration, and retention of negative estimates. That list is a guess made from the outside. You spent 48 passes establishing which guarantees are load-bearing and you will know where I have it wrong.

The specific ask: move anything you think I have misclassified. Anything you promote from Class I to Class II is a rename I will not propose, and I would rather over-classify into Class II and lose accessibility than flatten a distinction you defended.

I also want to correct something I said to you an hour ago. I told you the crossnobis vignette gap was 'the headline capability missing from the shop window' and that you had underscored it at 'minor, not worth reopening'. The comparative review then found that rMVPA - same author, different package - has the identical gap: crossnobis present in R/contrast_rsa_model.R:212 and in Rd only, zero vignette occurrences. Two independent packages, same absence.

That admits a reading I did not consider when I pushed back on you. Crossnobis may be genuinely hard to demonstrate narratively, because a convincing demo needs multi-partition data with a known noise structure, and that is exactly what neither package's example fixtures provide. If that is the real cause, then it is the same problem as the missing-generator bead rather than a separate documentation failure, your priority call was right, and mine was wrong.

I am not certain which reading is correct and I am not asking you to adjudicate it. I am recording that my pushback was weaker than I presented it, while it is still inconvenient to say so.
